title: Envelope
description: CloudEvents 1.0, JSON mode, with the four Blume extension attributes. Closed: publishers MUST NOT define additional extensions without registry approval, so an unrecognised attribute is a validation failure rather than a tolerated addition. The `data` member is validated separately against the event's own schema, resolved from `dataschema`.

id.description: ULID, Crockford base32. Monotonic within a source. The idempotency key, and the value of the `Nats-Msg-Id` header.

source.description: //blume.systems/<tenant>/<domain>/<asset-class>/<asset-id>. Ordering is guaranteed per source, not globally.

type.description: systems.blume.<domain>.<event-name>.<major>. The major token MUST equal the major of the semantic version in `dataschema`.

subject.description: CloudEvents subject: the asset the event is about. Distinct from `subject_ref`, which references a natural person and never appears here. Optional.

time.description: RFC 3339, UTC, millisecond precision. The time the fact occurred, not the time it was published.

datacontenttype.description: Always application/json. The bus carries no binary content modes.

dataschema.description: Absolute registry URI including the full semantic version. Every published version resolves permanently.

blumetenant.description: Duplicates the subject token so the envelope is self-describing off-bus.

blumeretention.description: Retention class. An event carries exactly one. Consumers MUST ignore unknown values.

blumetrace.description: W3C traceparent. Version 00; all-zero trace and span identifiers are invalid. The two `not` clauses express that, rather than a negative lookahead, because the Go validator compiles patterns with RE2 and RE2 has no lookahead. Do not simplify this back to `(?!0{32})`: it will not compile, and the failure reads like a library bug rather than a schema error.

blumeseq.description: Per-source monotonic counter. Gaps indicate loss.

data.description: Event payload. Validated against the schema named by `dataschema`.
